subject.title: fix(plugins): plugins.deny is bypassed by a mixed-case manifest id

question: Should mixed-case native plugin IDs remain a supported declared identity with a separate lowercase policy key, be canonicalized across every manifest/runtime/package identity surface, or be rejected as invalid?
rationale: The PR closes a security-relevant policy bypass, but the documentation currently describes exact manifest/runtime ID agreement without explicitly declaring lowercase-only IDs, so automation cannot choose the compatibility contract safely.

options.title: Separate declared and policy IDs
options.body: Keep the plugin’s declared ID intact while using a canonical lowercase identity for every policy and reserved-ID decision.

options.title: Canonicalize the whole contract
options.body: Lowercase manifest, runtime-export validation, package hints, registry records, and diagnostics together, with upgrade coverage for existing mixed-case plugins.

options.title: Reject mixed-case manifests
options.body: Fail manifest validation with an actionable error before activation, accepting the explicit compatibility break as security policy.

recommendation.title: Separate declared and policy IDs
recommendation.body: Keep the plugin’s declared ID intact while using a canonical lowercase identity for every policy and reserved-ID decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin manifest and activation-contract work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the public identity decision.
